acceptance_test_matrix: Empty range coverage asserts zero StoreVisitor invocations for SINGLE and DOUBLE store variants.
Single-key range coverage asserts inclusive bounds return exactly one present key and no absent key.
Full-keyspace range coverage asserts all present keys are visited in ascending key order without materializing results on the hot path.
Reverse scan coverage asserts descendingRange returns keys in descending order for SINGLE and DOUBLE variants.
Direct and mmap backend coverage confirms equivalent range semantics where both backends expose SINGLE and DOUBLE stores.
Configured QA gate coverage requires ./gradlew :store:test, ./qa/smoke.sh, and ./qa/regression.sh to pass, including the allocation gate for visitor hot paths.
assumptions: The range API belongs in the store module public surface alongside existing Stores facade and direct/mmap implementations unless design review finds an existing store API interface is the canonical owner.
Range bounds are inclusive for both ascending and descending scans.
Empty ranges must complete without StoreVisitor callbacks.
SINGLE and DOUBLE variants include direct and mmap-backed implementations where those classes expose the same store behavior.
Existing seqlock/read consistency semantics remain authoritative for slot reads during range scans.
Optional key-prefix filtering is out of scope unless it can be expressed without Consumer boxing, streams, temporary key wrappers, or visitor hot-path allocation.

acceptance_tests: Empty inclusive range invokes StoreVisitor zero times for SINGLE and DOUBLE stores.
Single-key inclusive range visits exactly that key when present and zero keys when absent.
Full-keyspace ascending range visits all present keys in ascending key order for SINGLE and DOUBLE stores.
Descending range visits matching keys in descending key order for SINGLE and DOUBLE stores without buffering allocations.
Direct and mmap SINGLE and DOUBLE implementations pass the same semantic tests.
Allocation-focused test or existing smoke allocation gate confirms no visitor hot-path allocation.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Range scans must preserve the existing store read protocol by using the same stable-slot or seqlock validation used by point reads, skipping unstable or absent slots according to current read semantics, and never exposing partially-read values to StoreVisitor.
forbidden_alternatives: Materializing matching keys or values into arrays, lists, streams, iterators, snapshots, or other collections before visiting.
Implementing descending scans by scanning ascending and buffering results for later replay.
Adding sorted-by-value lookup behavior, composite-key encodings, secondary-index files, or background index maintenance.
Changing mmap file format, slot layout, journal, checkpoint, or durability protocols for this feature.
Testing only direct stores, only mmap stores, or only one of SINGLE and DOUBLE variants.
hard_constraints: Visitor hot path must not allocate.
Range scans must not use java.util.function.Consumer, iterators, streams, lambda boxing, boxed Long/Object callback paths, or per-entry temporary collections.
Bounds are inclusive for ascending and descending scans.
SINGLE and DOUBLE variants must share semantics across direct and mmap backends.
Do not change existing point-read or write APIs except to add compatible range-scan surface.
Do not introduce sorted-by-value queries, composite keys, secondary indexes, persistent range indexes, or mmap format changes.
qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, and :store:test must pass before final PR handoff.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: store/src/main/java/com/joshorig/ull/lvc/store/ owns the public store API and facade wiring; store/src/main/java/com/joshorig/ull/lvc/store/direct/ owns direct SINGLE and DOUBLE scan loops; store/src/main/java/com/joshorig/ull/lvc/store/mmap/ owns mmap SINGLE and DOUBLE scan loops; docs/ documents public semantics; repo-memory/ records roadmap and decision notes; test roots own range fixtures and assertions only.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: Mmap-backed range scans are read-only over existing mapped slots and must not alter file layout, normalization, journal, checkpoint, recovery, or durability behavior.
design_contract.public_api: Add a zero-allocation StoreVisitor interface and inclusive ascendingRange and descendingRange range-scan methods for SINGLE and DOUBLE store surfaces, exposed through existing store package and facade conventions in store/src/main/java/com/joshorig/ull/lvc/store/. Visitor callbacks receive primitive key data and reusable or read-only value views consistent with existing store read semantics, without per-entry allocation.

final.problem_statement: Implement zero-allocation inclusive ascending and descending range scans for SINGLE and DOUBLE LVC stores using a StoreVisitor API, with coverage for empty ranges, single-key ranges, full-keyspace ranges, and reverse scans.
risk_register: Range ordering may differ from physical slot order if existing key-to-slot mapping is hash-like; design must confirm whether keyspace iteration is naturally ordered or requires bounded scan over numeric key domain without allocation.
Visitor callback value lifetime may be misunderstood; API docs must state whether slices are valid only during callback or follow existing read-only slice rules.
Descending scans can accidentally allocate by buffering ascending results; implementation must scan in descending key order directly.
Mmap and direct stores may duplicate scan logic and drift; shared helper extraction is allowed only if it does not add allocation or blur backend ownership.
Concurrent writes during range scans can expose unstable slots unless existing seqlock validation is reused consistently.
Optional prefix filtering can create boxing or object allocation if implemented with Consumer, Predicate, streams, or temporary key wrappers.
